score.notes: A confident, symmetric Mughal-leaning facade with a coherent base→body→crown reading: crenellated plinth, a two-register body of framed arched niches, and a crown of a central blue onion dome with gold finial flanked by two corner pavilion-turrets. The dominant terracotta-orange / supporting gold-frame / deep-lapis-blue accent scheme is disciplined and genuinely colorful — a clear, harmonious identity. The central arched portal with its glowing violet gradient is the strongest move, giving an unmistakable grand entrance and real temple presence. Detail is purposeful where it counts: recessed niches with arched gold surrounds, pilaster bays, and articulated crown pavilions read with actual relief depth. What holds each dimension back from exceptional, and I can name the improvements: the broad orange wall fields between niches stay flat, and the scattered purple specks across them read as pixel noise rather than intentional ornament rather than resolving the whole surface; the crown trio perches slightly small and detached atop a fairly plain box, so the massing is coherent but not inevitable. Strong across the board, not iconic — a very good build, but each measure has an easy lever left.
